clue.text: A thousand odd times is a lot

parts.note: K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand, as in 10K

indicators.note: odd here means strange or peculiar, telling us the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a thousand unusual occasions add up to quite a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal, not 'strange times'. 'Lot' is not 'many' but one's lot in life, one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lot is your fate or destiny, and kismet is the Turkish-derived word for fate.

clue.text: Wily monarch now imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means shut inside, so the word now is put within the word for the monarch

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A cunning king has now been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wily' looks like a description of the monarch, but it is the definition; 'imprisoned' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A knowing look is a sly, shrewd one, so knowing can mean crafty.

clue.text: Extent of usefulness on board

parts.note: read literally, the length of time goods remain usable while sitting on a board or ledge in a shop

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like how long someone stays useful on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a director or a ship; the board is really a shelf in a shop or store.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means the period a product can be stored before it spoils, literally its time on a shelf.

clue.text: Frenchman who couldn't adapt to a new regime?

definitions.text: Frenchman who couldn't adapt to a new regime?

indicators.note: adapting a thing to something new reshapes it, so the letters of the word regime are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who fled because he could not accept the Revolution's new government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapt to a new' rearranges REGIME, and the whole clue describes an aristocrat who left France after 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is someone who has left their country, especially a royalist who fled revolutionary France.

clue.text: Painting with rollers?

parts.note: rollers are not decorators' tools but big waves rolling in, so this is a picture showing waves

explanation.surface: Decorating a wall with a paint roller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painting with rollers' suggests decorating; rollers are long ocean waves and the painting is a picture of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture of the ocean, which would show rolling waves.

clue.text: Still divisible by two

explanation.surface: A number that is nevertheless divisible by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means still, as in 'even more', and an even number divides exactly by two.

clue.text: It looks impressive, but it's not working

explanation.surface: Something looks grand but does not function.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the workers on strike, not a broken machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking is eye-catching, and workers who are striking have downed tools in protest.

clue.text: Wide awake to a siren call

explanation.surface: Being jolted fully awake by the wail of a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means watchful and fully awake, and an alert is also a warning signal such as an air-raid siren.

clue.text: Win the right to retain article of terracotta

indicators.note: retaining something means holding it within, so the word for the article goes inside the other word

parts.note: to earn something is to win the right to it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone wins permission to keep a piece of terracotta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' is the container signal; 'Win the right' is one piece, not WIN plus R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is baked clay, and earthen means made of clay or baked earth.

clue.text: In opera Eugene shows singular spirit

parts.note: singular means one in number
gin is a spirit, a distilled drink

explanation.surface: In an opera, the hero Eugene displays a unique character.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Onegin is Tchaikovsky's opera based on Pushkin's verse novel; 'spirit' is the drink, not his mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Onegin is the surname of Eugene, the title character of Tchaikovsky's opera.

clue.text: Listen repeatedly for a sign of approval

indicators.note: repeatedly means said more than once, so the synonym of listen appears twice

parts.note: to hear is to listen

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep listening for a signal that something is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles HEAR. The cry is the British parliamentary shout of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled call is a cry of agreement, as shouted by MPs in the House of Commons when backing a speaker.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in source of sugar and spice

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so the currency goes inside the plant

parts.note: sugar cane is a source of sugar
the yen is Japan's currency, foreign money to a British solver

explanation.surface: Overseas cash put into the sugar and spice trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance but is the container signal; the sugar source is the plant, not beet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a spice.

clue.text: Teach a pupil without discipline

parts.note: to inform is to tell or teach
L stands for learner, a pupil, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Instructing a student who lacks self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' is a learner, giving L, not part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual, without formality or strict rules of conduct.

clue.text: Draw south by boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Someone sketches the coast going south by boat, or travels that way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is the definition, a verb meaning to make a quick drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a rough drawing is to outline a picture quickly.

clue.text: Soft soap and a face-cloth

explanation.surface: Gentle soap and a washcloth for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' is not a toiletry but flattery or evasive talk, the British sense of flannel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for flattering or evasive talk, and it also names a small cloth for washing the face.

clue.text: Courage needed on icy roads

explanation.surface: Bravery is required when driving on frozen roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is pluck and determination, and it is also the coarse sand spread on roads in winter.

clue.text: Point to one duke or another

definitions.text: Point to one duke or another

parts.words: Point to one duke or another
parts.note: a single name that can indicate one famous duke, or something else that bears his name

explanation.surface: Indicating a particular duke, or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington lent his title to the rubber boot, the beef dish and New Zealand's capital, so the name points to the duke or to another thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley was the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo, and many things carry the same title.

clue.text: Striker on trial in international game

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the striker's word comes beside the trial's word

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A footballer is given a trial ahead of an international fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer but is the match you strike. A test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national sides, especially in cricket or rugby.

clue.text: Being solvent, her career is taking off

explanation.surface: Being financially secure, a woman finds her career taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' looks like having money but is the liquid for removing paint; 'taking off' is undressing, not success.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is a chemical that removes paint or varnish, and also a performer who undresses for an audience.

clue.text: "Tauten line" ordered by naval officer

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of the quoted words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval officer barks the order to tighten a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a naval command, but it signals that TAUTEN LINE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned rank in the navy, just below lieutenant commander.

clue.text: Hide article in play

indicators.note: in places the article within the title of the play

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's play
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Concealing an item somewhere in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is the noun, an animal's skin, not the verb to conceal; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, which is what a hide becomes.

clue.text: Once-powerful Russian arts organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of the word arts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A formerly mighty Russian body that ran the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like a body or company but signals rearranging ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Order 18 down to make reparation

explanation.surface: Telling someone to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cross-reference: the performer at 18 down has undressed, so you would tell her to put her clothes back on.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling an undressed performer to put on clothes again is to tell her to dress once more; redress also means to put a wrong right.

clue.text: Murder mother for the estate

annotationWithheld.why: Murder mother for the estate: DO IN (murder) around MA (mother) gives the answer, but no clue word signals the insertion; 'for' is a link, so the clue as held may have lost a word

clue.text: Under treatment, impart personal depression

indicators.note: something under treatment is being worked on and changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient receiving therapy confides a private gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal depression' is not a mood but a hollow in one's own body. 'Under treatment' rearranges IMPART.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder where the arm joins the body is a depression of one's own anatomy.

clue.text: Be entitled to credit

explanation.surface: Someone deserves praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, and merit is also credit or praise for worth.

clue.text: Shaped up again-to a more moral life?

explanation.surface: A sinner is reshaped and turned towards a more virtuous way of living.
explanation.definitionFit: Reformed means formed anew, given a fresh shape, and also improved in character after giving up bad ways.

clue.text: A footnote at the end of the service in church

parts.note: PS stands for postscript, a note added at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: at the end of points to the final letter of the word service

explanation.surface: A footnote added at the close of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in church' defines a part of a church, the semicircular recess at the east end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church building, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: A piece for brass and wind instruments

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument
a pipe is a simple wind instrument

explanation.surface: A musical composition scored for brass and woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The piece is a lively sailors' dance tune, traditionally played on a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively dance tune, a short musical composition associated with sailors.

clue.text: The stock market is the place to buy them

definitions.text: The stock market is the place to buy them

parts.words: The stock market is the place to buy them
parts.note: the stock is not shares but livestock, sold at a farm market

explanation.surface: A broker's advice that shares should be bought on the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock market' suggests finance; here it is a livestock market where farm animals are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are farm livestock, bought and sold at a livestock market.

clue.text: Made a comeback and was elected

explanation.surface: A politician staged a comeback and won the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Returned means came back, and a candidate returned to Parliament has been elected.

clue.text: Moves in an unfinished game on board

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its ending, so the last letter of the board game is dropped

parts.note: chess is a game played on a board

explanation.surface: Making moves in a chess game that has not been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moves' is a verb meaning creeps forward slowly, not chess moves. 'unfinished' drops the last S of CHESS, leaving CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to advance very slowly, a little at a time.
